role: UIStateCache: @MainActor singleton read model holding last dashboard and fitness display snapshots, persisted as JSON in Application Support so tabs paint instantly at cold start.
types: UIStateCache.RecentDaySnapshot / DashboardSnapshot / FitnessSnapshot: struct (Codable) — display values; FitnessSnapshot.day (optional, decodes absent as nil) dates its today* figures
UIStateCache.Store: struct (private, Codable) — on-disk envelope with schema
state: file:ApplicationSupport/UIStateCache.json (schema 1, JSON sealed with the app's key via JSONFileSeal.app; a plain-JSON file from a build that did not seal it is read and replaced sealed)
toplevel: static shared, schemaVersion = 1, persistenceURL lazy closure, writeQueue serial queue.

units.does: Stores a new dashboard snapshot and persists it when it differs from the current one.
Stores a new fitness snapshot and persists it when changed.

Delete All My Data: sets dashboard and fitness to nil, then (when the Application Support URL resolved) queues on the serial write queue, behind any write still pending, a removal of UIStateCache.json if it exists (failure logged through attempt).

branches.cond: file absent when the queued block runs

units.does: Lazy static: Application Support directory (created if needed) + UIStateCache.json; nil when the directory cannot be obtained.

branches.effect: false: nil (cache never persists or loads)

units.entry: Lazy creation of UIStateCache.shared via AppDependencies.storage.uiStateCache

units.does: Snapshots both values and, on the serial writeQueue, encodes and seals them with JSONFileSeal.app.sealJSON (the app's key) and writes the bytes atomically with completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication; when the seal (no key) or the write fails nothing is written and a warning is logged — the cache is rebuilt from live data, so there is no plain fallback.

branches.effect: catch: warning log, nothing written; next launch starts without a seed

units.does: When UIStateCache.json exists, reads it and opens and decodes it with JSONFileSeal.app.openJSON (sealed bytes decrypted, plain JSON from a build that did not seal it read as is); restores dashboard/fitness when schema == 1. A read, open or decode failure is logged through attempt and leaves both nil; a missing file or schema mismatch leaves both nil silently.

branches.cond: URL, data, decode and schema all succeed
branches.effect: false: return with empty cache; true: assign and log
